d: It's winter and the pond's frozen and that means Strawberry and friends can ice skate! They decide to showcase their talents at an Ice Dance Show. But just then, a new kid named Apricot shows up.
When Strawberry & her friends decide to put on a talent show, they plan to enter themselves as a band, The Strawberry Jams!
Strawberry and her friends are getting the band back together to perform at a local festival, but Ginger Snap is out of town.
Strawberry Shortcake has always dreamed of seeing a certain rare flower, which only blooms once every ten years - and then only for a day!
After an accidental wager with Purple Pieman, Strawberry sets off to prove that she can go around the world in 80 days.
One night, as Strawberry & Friends gaze at the stars, they talk about what they want to be when they grow up.
As Strawberry & Friends visit a Career Fair, they ponder their own futures. They all have thoughts on the jobs they would like: teacher, firefighter, doctor, etc.
Annie Oatmeal hires both Strawberry Shortcake and Angel Cake to work at her dude ranch. Things get complicated when there's a competition to decide which Ranch Hand runs the Best Bunkhouse.

Strawberry gets an unsettling message from her friend Caramel Corn, who owns a quaint little farm out in the Strawberryland countryside. Things aren't going so well for Caramel Corn: her farm animals seem to be running away.
It's a retelling of L. Frank Baum's classic "Wonderful Wizard of Oz" - told from Pupcake's point of view.
When Strawberry gets an urgent plea to return to Oz, she finds that there's an environmental disaster.
It's a retelling of "Sleeping Beauty" - but our focus is on the fairy that didn't get her invitation.
This is the story of "Rapunzel", but with a twist. Princess Rapunzel (Rainbow Sherbet) has always preferred being called Rap and liked doing things her way.

Strawberry Shortcake's childhood friend, Lime Lite, has hit it big in Berrywood, movie capital of Strawberryland. Unfortunately, she's become a bit of a diva in the process, and her self-centered behavior is about to cut her career short.
